review_markdown: The contract needs three bounded repairs before registration. Its retained-debt model follows the pinned C branch, and U3 is resolved by the coordinator manifest. This verdict concerns contract readiness only; it accepts no billing implementation or family closure.

findings.trigger: Call record_bill_terms twice for the same valid full-generation unpaid item, with identical or changed terms.
findings.evidence: contract.json api.admission defines item/ledger validation but gives no existing-receipt result. representation.invariants permits at most one receipt, while representation.liability freezes terms at admission. Replacing the existing entry would satisfy uniqueness while changing frozen liability.
findings.consequence: Implementations can disagree between rejection, idempotence and replacement; a second admission can change quantity, price or creditor without an accepted reconciliation route.
findings.repair: Define both repeated-admission outcomes explicitly. Reject changed terms atomically; choose rejection or exact idempotence for identical terms. Specify the error/result and add complete-state/RNG/events/time comparisons. Permit no receipt replacement under this child.

findings.trigger: After successful receipt admission, invoke existing remove_unpaid directly or reach it through Pay.
findings.evidence: world.rs:680 removes the compatibility tuple only. economy.rs:117–140 calculates current projected prices and calls remove_unpaid. The proposed API1 allowlist expressly preserves that body, yet global live_terms requires a corresponding unpaid owner and SAVE1 rejects dangling receipts.
findings.consequence: An existing public path can leave admitted terms without their ledger entry, omit liability from tuple-based views, or make a previously valid world fail save/load validation. Pay also lacks a defined relationship to the frozen receipt amount.
findings.repair: Specify and enforce a bounded policy for existing ledger-clearing paths while live receipts exist. Either refuse unsupported settlement atomically pending DG06-bill-settlement, or separately authorize a source-backed synchronized route. Enumerate any additional existing body before implementation approval; keep consumed debt untouched. Add admission→clearing/Pay→view/save/disposal coverage without expanding into a full shop audit.

findings.trigger: Root prepares BILL-SAVE1’s required oldpack/schema/hash acceptance evidence.
findings.evidence: compatibility.pack_schema_hash assigns exact fixture IDs and scratch comparisons to SAVE1 but leaves the generation manifest for later root collection. validation.focused_future_commands supplies package tests without concrete schema-generation, canonical-hash or scratch-comparison argv.
findings.consequence: Mandatory compatibility exits are not reproducible from this packet, and implementations can select different fixtures or comparison procedures.
findings.repair: Supply the minimal SAVE1 fixture IDs, exact generation/hash/comparison argv, scratch destinations, expected unchanged outputs and failure exits. Assign the focused commands to API1 versus SAVE1. Keep production outputs and every existing assertion/setup frozen; no execution is required for this repair.

checks.name: Bindings and authority
checks.evidence: Native HEAD matches 8f44a7a9f7a1536e2c5a21ec47596777ac705fc0. Checked consumed hashes and evidence snippet bindings. C bytes came exclusively from pinned git show. Coordinator archive verification was not repeated.

checks.name: Retained liability and source scope
checks.evidence: shk.c:1224–1233 retains the object and leaves receipt price/bquan unchanged; 4244–4246 uses bquan for consumed liability. Literal q1/q3 totals are 40/120. Unknown historical terms remain explicit. Unequal live/billed quantities are explicitly rejected and deferred to DG06-bill-merge-partial.

checks.name: Save/cache design
checks.evidence: Global live terms retain cached full handles and remap through the restored item_map; consumed origins/creditors remain historical. Validation precedes timer catchup. No StoredLevel field or existing test-constructor edits are proposed. Modern, absent and explicit-empty owners have required future coverage.

checks.name: Allowlist and prerequisites
checks.evidence: Named API1/SAVE1 files and existing bodies match inspected owners. API1→SAVE1→LIFE activation introduces no stated cycle. LIFE cleanup needs separate acceptance; IN1/D1/PRE and adapter/frontend exits remain mandatory.

checks.name: U3 and historical gates
checks.evidence: Durable harness SHA matches the root manifest; its parsed 12 command vectors match exactly. Prior accepted.json records 1026 tests/12 checks and the bound digest. These are historical evidence, not fresh execution.

checks.name: Deferred scope and compatibility
checks.evidence: Settlement/history/account/partial/nonwand/nonrepresented-reference branches have successors under existing families. All53/543 scope, frozen assertions, exact future golden permission, dependency restrictions and deterministic ordering remain preserved.

handoff: Return F1–F3 to the author for bounded contract repair and fresh review. Root should register children, publish and commit only after contract readiness passes.
usage_note: Independent read-only semantic review. No edits, Cargo/builds, C/Lua execution, agents or gate-harness execution.
